deepdive.sec: Onshore Wind Turbine OEM + Renewable EPC / Project Development

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash INR 2,384 cr; net worth INR 9,464 cr — exceptional balance-sheet strength, deleveraged.
- Working-capital build-up mainly PSU receivables, anticipated and priced into tenders; largely serviced via non-fund-based limits; WC days could improve in secular growth.
- DevCo land capital ring-fenced ~INR 300 cr threshold. No dividend mention.
- DTA recognition boosts book PAT but is non-cash.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- DSM tightening (CERC plus/minus 15→10%; new projects on fossil-fuel deviation from 1-Apr-2026) — currently stayed but mgmt expects implementation; turbine performance/penalty risk, mitigated by forecasting service.
- Working-capital / PSU receivables stretch; OCF (~INR 12 bn) well below EBITDA (~INR 30 bn) for FY26.
- Order intake lumpy — Q4 intake "tad muted"; EPC deals take longer to close.
- INR depreciation / commodity (steel) — partly pass-through, residual exposure.
- Execution: 971-975 MW erected-but-not-commissioned (~350 MW awaiting customer last-mile).
- New CEO (Ajay Kapur) transition; APERC tariff approval pending for 775 MW FDRE; FDRE/solar-BESS strategy unproven for Suzlon.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- Confident, delivery-focused; J.P.C explicitly scored FY26 against prior commitments (60% growth promised → 63% EBITDA, 65% WTG rev) — high accountability.
- New CEO Ajay Kapur (ex-Ambuja Cements MD) signals professionalization; emphasis on leading vs lagging indicators, line-org rejuvenation.
- Resisted giving hard FY27 delivery guidance ("putting words in my mouth") — disciplined but slightly opaque; acknowledged investor request for monthly installation data, "will evaluate."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Reported PAT inflated by INR 742 cr DTA (FY) / Q4 reported PAT INR 281 cr ex-adjustment — cash earnings materially lower than headline PAT.
- The strategic crux is the shift from product OEM to project developer (DevCo): margin/order-book lumpiness near-term but converts Suzlon into the sector's execution-bottleneck solver.
- Evening peak demand data (solar 0%, wind 21% contribution) is mgmt's core bull case for structural FDRE/wind bid revival.
- Europe re-entry interest is for legacy 2-3 MW series, not just new Blue Sky turbines — faster monetization optionality.
- Exceptional INR 70 cr is SE Forge arbitration win (in favour), NOT an OMS problem as analysts feared.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
- **WTG**: rev INR 14,040 cr FY (+65%), contribution margin 24.5%. 4.5 GW manufacturing capacity fully operational; adding 3 AI-enabled smart blade factories.
- **OMS (Renom)**: 15.7+ GW under management India, machine availability >95%; AUM growing on fleet additions. Q2 EBITDA dip recouped — full-year OMS EBITDA 40.5% (was flagged one-off).
- **SE Forge**: rev INR 597 cr (+22%), EBITDA INR 119 cr (+61%), domestic + export driven; INR 70 cr exceptional arbitration gain.
- **EPC / DevCo**: new growth engine; land-to-commissioning turnkey; full FDRE (RE) stack intent vs just wind portion.
- **Exports / Blue Sky**: re-entry into Europe via Spain launch (S175, S163 turbines); strong developer/IPP/utility interest also for legacy 2 MW & 3 MW series; mgmt sees future big revenue + bottom-line driver.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body:
- Consol EBITDA margin 18.1% (+100 bps YoY); WTG contribution margin 24.5%.
- Steel largely pass-through (except some PSU contracts); FX partly pass-through; cost-management drives mitigate INR depreciation impact.
- Levers: S144 scale (9 GW) enabling supplier renegotiation; supply diversification + Make-in-India; R&D-led value engineering; annual cost-cut target.
- Mgmt: WTG margins shouldn't materially fall FY27; unsure how much pricing can be raised — relies on business-model reorientation (EPC + DevCo).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
**This quarter (Q4 FY26):**
- Record Q4 deliveries 830 MW; FY26 deliveries 2,456 MW (+58%); record FY revenue INR 16,679 cr (+54%).
- New Group CEO Ajay Kapur (ex-Ambuja) joined; J.P.C moved to Group Executive Counsel.
- Order book up 5.0→5.9 GW YoY; EPC share rose 20%→28% in H2; S144 intake ~9 GW.
- AP PIA extended 24 months — 2.1 GW dev rights revived (775 MW→FDRE, 1,325 MW→EPC).
- DTA recognition INR 742 cr lifted FY PAT to INR 3,153 cr; net cash INR 2,384 cr.
- Blue Sky European platform launched in Spain (S175, S163).
- SE Forge arbitration win INR 70 cr exceptional; OMS EBITDA recouped to 40.5% FY.

**Next-quarter watch items:**
- First EPC order announcements from AP DevCo pipeline (expected "from June onwards").
- APERC tariff finalization for 775 MW FDRE PPA + client/SPV takeover.
- NTPC turnkey EPC awards (540 MW + 2,000 MW AP) closure.
- DSM stay outcome and forecasting-service rollout.
- Commissioning conversion of 971-975 MW erected backlog; working-capital / receivables trend.
- Sunsure order scale-in; whether mgmt starts disclosing monthly installation numbers.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log

outlook.body:
- Industry installations: ~8 GW FY27, ~10 GW FY28, ~15 GW by FY30/31 (Suzlon expects to track market +/-).
- Mgmt declined to give absolute FY27 delivery number; pointed to past trend (700→1,550→2,456 MW) and "positive trend to continue."
- EPC share of order book: 28% now → targeting 50% by FY28.
- WTG margins: "don't think materially can go down" in FY27; steel largely pass-through.
- EPC order closures from AP DevCo pipeline expected to start being announced "from June onwards."
- Capex run-rate ~INR 600 cr +/- 50 over next 3-4 years (vs ~INR 550 cr FY26).
- DTA: only deferred-tax CHARGE (non-cash) hits P&L next 2 years; ~INR 3,000-3,500 cr unrecognized DTA remaining.
outlook.title: Guidance (verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Order book 5.9 GW; 66% C&I + PSU. Post-quarter Sunsure order takes effective book to ~6 GW.
- S144 (3.X MW) cumulative order intake ~9 GW — flagship platform.
- DevCo identified-sites pipeline 22-23 GW; ~8 GW in active development (land acquisition / land contracts signed). "Slightly higher" now.
- AP PIA: 2.1 GW development rights, extended 24 months by new AP govt (Apr). 775 MW with PPA → being converted to FDRE (APERC tariff pending); balance 1,325 MW → firm EPC contracts to be monetized over next 6 months from June.
- NTPC moving from split contracts (BOP + WTG) to turnkey EPC: 215 MW in AP already, plus expected 540 MW + 2,000 MW in AP. Mgmt sees Suzlon strong in PSU EPC.
- ArcelorMittal EPC order came out of the DevCo pipeline.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- DevCo / land-bank development model — convert dynamic 22-23 GW identified sites into EPC contracts; "engine for growth of the sector," unlocks execution bottleneck.
- FDRE / hybrid (wind + solar + BESS) — intent to supply full RE stack; solar/BESS "very much on agenda" but no acquisition imminent; strategy (asset-light vs invest) TBD.
- Scheduling & forecasting service — monetizing DSM tightening (plus/minus 15% → 10%) as add-on service; collaborating with international players.
- European/export re-entry via Blue Sky; repowering opportunity (India fleet 56 GW installed, FY26 installs highest since 2017).
- RE parks with transferable GNA connectivity — working with GoI on regulation change.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: India's dominant onshore wind OEM is pivoting from pure turbine supply to integrated EPC + DevCo land-bank developer, riding a multi-year wind-installation upcycle (6 GW industry FY26 → 10-15 GW medium-term) with a record-profitable, net-cash balance sheet.
